messages:
Ryan S.: heads-up — customer on the POC is hitting a 413 / request-too-large when we send their whole convo + docs. they say it worked on their local Llama2 but not on rw-32k here.
Alex P.: ok can you paste the raw request size and which endpoint? hosted or dedicated?
Ryan S.: hosted, using /v1/chat/completions (streaming off). payload ~ 1.1MB gzipped, ~7.2MB uncompressed. model=rw-32k. error shows `HTTP 413 Payload Too Large`.
Mira S.: 1.1MB gzipped should normally be fine but depends on gateway limits. are they including large base64 attachments or just text?
Ryan S.: just text — long transcripts + product docs. they concat everything into messages.
Sam T.: quick checklist: 1) confirm Content-Length header from client 2) any proxy (nginx, app gateway) with smaller body limit? 3) are they hitting per-request token window vs upload limit?
Kai L.: Also confirm they aren't sending a single message > model context window. If the request expands to >32768 tokens we'll truncate server-side. But that usually returns a shorter completion, not 413. 413 is ingress body size.
Ryan S.: customer says they can't change their client easily. asked for a best-practice workaround.
Alex P.: short-term: recommend server-side chunking on our side — i.e., upload documents as embeddings + do retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) before calling chat. That reduces payload drastically.
Mira S.: alternate: enable streaming on client and send earlier tokens, but streaming doesn't help body size for initial request.
Sam T.: can we advise them to gzip? they already gzipped. do we accept Transfer-Encoding: chunked?
Kai L.: yes we support chunked encoding. If their gzipped size is 1.1MB, file likely ok. but many infra frontends have hard limits (often 1MB). I'll ask infra to check the load balancer/nginx default body size for hosted cluster for this customer region. @Riley-bot can you pull recent nginx error logs for 1798-prod?
Riley-bot: pulling logs for tag=1798-prod, time=+/-30m — found several 413 entries for client IP 52.23.145.9 at 2026-11-02T14:12:09Z.
Alex P.: good catch. so it's LB rejecting. Kai, can infra bump client_max_body_size or add a route exception?
Kai L.: I can add a temporary route config to 5MB while we coordinate with the customer. Will update in 20m.
Ryan S.: customer also worried about context truncation when they try splitting — they want guidance on chunking semantics to keep retrieval order.
Sam T.: advise: chunk docs into ~2–4k token windows with overlaps (256–512 tokens) for RAG. store embeddings, then on query do top-k retrieval and pass only top 3–5 docs plus convo. That keeps chat payload < 200KB typically.
Mira S.: also mention prefix caching: if there are repeating system messages, store as prefix and reference it (we have prefix IDs for Redwood Dedicated customers). For hosted, suggest passing the system once and then use a session-level KV on client.
Alex P.: for pricing & POC expectations — if they switch to RAG we can show cost projection comparing sending full context vs embeddings+retrieval. I can run numbers if they share typical token counts.
Ryan S.: they sent a sample of 250k characters (~40k tokens).
Sam T.: 40k tokens > 32k window — must do RAG or truncate. We'll recommend a two-phase approach: 1) short-term LB bump so POC continues; 2) mid-term implement RAG + embeddings; 3) long-term consider Dedicated with custom LB and higher body limits and local prefix cache.
Kai L.: infrastructure update: temporary route exception deployed to region-us-west-2; clients from that account should stop seeing 413s. Monitoring for 10m.
Ryan S.: confirmed with customer — 413s stopped. thanks. they still need docs for chunking + sample code.
Alex P.: I'll send a short guide and a sample Node/py snippet showing: gzip, chunk -> embed -> retrieve -> call chat with top-k. keep it minimal.
Mira S.: sample snippet idea: `# pseudo
chunks = chunk_text(doc, max_tokens=3000, overlap=512)
embs = embed(chunks)
index.add(embs)`
Sam T.: also add guidance about re-ranking and prompt templates to reduce hallucination when using RAG.
Ryan S.: can someone draft the guide? I'll loop in the customer's security contact — they also asked about encrypt-at-rest for embeddings and retention policy.
Kai L.: retention/embeddings: hosted stores embeddings encrypted at rest (KMS). we can share our retention docs. I'll attach the RCA link.
Alex P.: assigning follow-ups: Alex -> write guide + cost projection; Kai -> confirm retention/KMS doc + infra LB change ticket; Sam -> sample code + prompt templates; Mira -> quick email to customer explaining short-term LB change and mid-term plan. Ryan -> coordinate with customer and collect token stats.
Ryan S.: perfect. I'll update the SLACK thread with customer sign-off once guide shared. :thumbsup:
